full bench on a shallow clone panicked (divide by zero) in repo-history after minutes: its corpora come from pinned commits a shallow clone lacks; now checks each pinned commit's whole history first and exits 2 with git fetch --unshallow; scores unchanged

append-only event log (G graph of sequence labels), idempotency view and last-write-wins kv view from existing objects; April fold tests as laws; every append rebuilt the views (1,000 single appends 6.2 s); scores unchanged
graph_edit re-cuts only the chunks edits fall in (root equals put_graph); views record their log position; 1,000 single appends 6.3 to 3.1 s; objects and bytes unchanged; scores unchanged

Keys::Any for ids and kv (a real 64-bit label-key collision kept and rebuilt); graph_edit reads only its path: one edit at 10M keys 94-105 ms to 2.2-2.4 ms, upper chunks read 1,321 to 3; scores unchanged
GET/HEAD under /dav/results/ send Cache-Control: no-cache (ETag and Last-Modified kept, 304s included): fetchers showed the 02:07 self-test results after the 6:00 run; other files unchanged

Store backends as options (packs, SQLite, LMDB, redb, fjall, RocksDB); packs: 769 MB/s writes, 2 flushes and 2 files per commit (files 66 and 25), 372 MB for 1M objects (files 4.1 GB), open 279 ms at 10M; 500 kills lost nothing; FsStore ref lock no longer wedges after a kill

ingest dropped a group's stored bytes after anti-unifying a new file with it (fill recorded, members read stored bytes): 4 ingests under distinct refs left 149 objects failing fsck; apply_candidate now keeps anything another encoding needs (dictionary, group, Q/M context); no format change

read_range asked the store for a leaf twice (a 4 KiB range of a 1 MB png fetched 2.2 MB, now 1.1); Office ranges rebuild the container (docx 31, pptx 59 reads), one part read by id fetches 2.76 MB against 18.9 MB whole; Markdown sections in groups save nothing
path lookup 2 reads by tree walk, 4 with a path index; db get 10 reads, 2.4 with a chunk cache; incoming links by scan 113k reads and 340 ms, by a reverse view 8 reads and 1 ms (33.9 MB view)
capability check 77 ns, reachable-set check 20 ns, tree-path proof 8 us; 29 internal objects serve 2+ of 24 tenants (one serves all), so checks belong at the file layer
goal search fetches about the matched files (invoice 195 KB, 2.8 ms); 2-character terms read everything (7.3 MB); windows give a model 6x fewer bytes but refetch groups without a cache

ReadSession shares decoded objects across one request's reads: all text files 7.31 to 5.30 MB fetched; goal windows now under the matched files whole (invoice 257 to 166 KB, files 184); 238 Office files 18.9 to 2.68 MB in one session

ingest checked every stored object before dropping a superseded copy, so one view update after a one-file commit read 3.68 GB (16 scans of the store); needed_index keeps that set in memory: 1.9 MB, 546 to 164 ms; same stored objects; off by default (single writer)

the first read of a derived file and any first has_content read all 229 MB of the store (1,907 reads) to build the ledger; the first write then reads 265 MB more for the seed index (2.0 s); a ledger cache would be 159 KB, 0.1 ms to load, but is an on-disk addition

seed_scope bounds the matcher's seed index to some contents' closure: a one-file edit's first write 238 MB / 1.7 s to 0.69 MB / 8.8 ms with the same bytes stored; scoped writes stored 2.9 KB vs 16.2 KB and 8.5 KB vs 21.8 KB (4 candidates per seed fill up on the whole store); off by default

one- and two-byte searches read every file (E127); with a trigram index they now take the posting lists of every trigram holding the pattern plus the contents under three bytes: "Q3" 7.1 MB / 40 ms to 0.70 MB / 12.6 ms, same results; no new structure

one goal end to end (short-term search, windows to a model, edit 5 files, commit, view update): fresh handle 9.22 GB / 2.9 s with defaults, 554 MB / 0.87 s with the recommended options; second goal on the handle 932 MB to 6.3 MB; seed_scope now follows named trees and view chunks (404 KB to 237 KB per view update) and set_seed_scope rescopes a handle
with needed_index on, the ledger's pass over every stored object also builds the needed index, so a fresh handle reads the store once: E133's first goal 554 MB to 324 MB fetched, same bytes written

Store::read_head lets the ledger and needed-index pass fetch 256-byte heads: a fresh handle's first lookup 229 MB to 192 KB with the same requests; the recommended first goal 324 MB to 94 MB, same bytes written

FsStore listings and the seed index in id order, so the same writes store the same encodings in every run and on every filesystem; goal runs now write identical bytes, ingest output and bench bytes unchanged

seed_scope set to the files a goal reads and edits (plus the trees and view chunks it replaces) instead of their folders: E133's first goal 94 MB / 797 ms to 7.7 MB / 318 ms, slightly fewer bytes written

Repo::read_memo (off by default, --read-memo) keeps the stored contents one tree, view or content write reads until it returns: E133's first goal 7.7 MB to 4.5 MB, its view update 3.85 MB to 1.01 MB, next goal 5.7 MB to 3.3 MB, identical objects stored

the recommended goal on real stores: first goal 4.5 MB in 735 ms on files, 351 ms on packs (PackStore::read_head added), 291 ms in memory; on files the view update syncs 425 objects; merges exp/122 so one branch holds all

Grant (src/grant.rs): per goal, read and write byte ranges of named file versions, sealed with keyed BLAKE3; Q3 goal exposes 16.7 KB of 347 KB; edit check 14 to 33 us; refuses all 70 out-of-window edits a file grant allows; reads fetch the same (groups decode whole)

Repo::replace_hints (off by default): with a scope, old trees and view chunks an edit reads join the seed index, so the scope names only the edited files: first goal 4.5 to 2.75 MB, next goal 3.3 to 1.2 MB, first write 1.78 MB to 189 KB, slightly fewer bytes written
ReadSession::search: a goal searches and reads in one session, so the read stage fetches nothing: first goal 2.50 to 2.04 MB, next goal 1.23 to 1.14 MB; 269 KB per goal is the search index load

read_memo also covers template candidates (each similar chunk was read twice per edit): recommended first goal 2.04 to 1.59 MB, next goal 1.14 to 0.78 MB; view update 906 to 522 KB; bytes written unchanged

Repo::object_templates (on by default): off, tree and view chunks are planned only as slices: first goal writes 250 to 86 KB and the store grows less (72 against 76 KB), 332 to 159 ms on packs; edits only add objects

Repo::begin_batch/end_batch/keep_read and ReadSession::into_contents: a goal's writes share one memo, handed the files it read; edit stage 414 to 70 KB, first goal 1.48 to 1.13 MB; the index build now joins the memo; bytes written unchanged
tree and view chunks stored plain: view update reads 405 to 393 KB but writes 72 to 391 KB; five times the growth for 3% fewer reads

Store::stored_len (default reads; Mem, Fs, Pack answer without reading): a batch handed its files reads nothing for template costs; edit stage 70 to 8 KB, first goal 1.13 to 1.07 MB, next goal 744 to 693 KB; writes unchanged

Repo::graph_prefix_pending/graph_node_pending: a view's new edges kept pending, folded every few goals; view update per goal 405 to 22 KB (150 to 37 ms on packs); one fold for two goals reads 445 KB against 744 KB; same final root; smaller view chunks measured and dropped

Repo::exact_short_search (off): patterns of 1-3 bytes answered from trigram postings without decoding; search 655 to 269 KB (index only), same matches; window range reads still fetch whole files (385 KB for 16.7 KB of windows)

seekable frames with a BLAKE3 outboard (measured, not stored): 4 KiB frames halve window reads (Q3 106 to 51 KB) for +55% text storage; 16 KiB frames +11% for 4%; not worth a format addition for small files
Repo::group_size (64 KiB default), --group-size: 16 KiB groups halve a goal's file reads (Q3 385 to 208 KB, AI 82 to 53 KB) for north +2.1% (0.3035 to 0.3100, over tolerance as a default)
search index decoded once per handle and reused (goal.rs config only): next goal 358 to 89 KB, 60 KB with 16 KiB groups; same matches, writes and view root
cutters over 534 text files: paragraph blocks dedup 1.24 (805 shared, fan-out 52); zstd over distinct fragments about 157 KB for every cutter, so cuts are for edits, not storage
new bytes per md edit: whole 740-860, blocks 115-176 (5.6-7.6 refs), CDC 256 201-367, lines 0-101 but 27-30 refs; kernel put_content 139-194

csv plus residual sidecar stored, json and md rendered on read: -43% on text formats, -1.8% with office files, 24/24 exact; render 241 ms at 10k rows against 6-11 ms read: archive option

one md edit to html and docx by splices: 58 ms against 134 ms re-render, 72/72 exact; stored as files 2,340 B per edit, html as fragments 3,210 B: store renders plain
ids by position, seams implied, 2 crossing trigrams per seam: 185,690 against 280,615 B, 0.093 ms per query, exact for any pattern length; update 0.24 ms
docx splices for inserted and deleted blocks, headings and lists with bookmarks, list ids and numbering.xml rebuilt: 168/168 whole .docx identical; deletes 2.8 ms against 77 ms
backends::hybrid (store-rocksdb): RefsHybrid and IndexHybrid; flushes per commit 2 and 1.5 against packs' 2 and a rename; 1M open 252 and 663 ms against 205; 100 kills clean; options, not a winner

PackOptions::ref_log (off): refs as records in the open pack, one flush and no rename a commit; swap p50 495 to 143 us; 100 kills clean; format addition (ref records, refs.snap); seal now syncs the packs directory

10M objects: packs with lazy_checkpoint and ref_log open in 2 ms (packs 330 to 440 ms, RocksDB 3.6 s first then 22 ms), 3.72 GB against RocksDB 4.32, build 93 s against 236; cold read p50 about 200 us against 150 for packs

store-level kills over 10M objects (crash-store phase, on exp/176): packs-fast and packs 30 of 30 clean each, nothing acknowledged lost; packs-fast 1.8x the commits; reopen p50 16 and 13 ms; the Repo-level test made no commits at 10M (E178)

backends::GroupCommit and PackStore::stage_ref: writers share one flush; 16 writers 3,800-4,300 to 12,500-15,500 commits/s, 8 commits a flush, p99 about 80 to 2 ms; 60 kills clean; needs the ref log

one db commit through the Repo on a fresh handle: defaults 10 ms p50 but a drop reads the whole store (2.2 s at 1M); needed_index first commit 7.7 s at 1M then 13 ms; with an empty seed scope 6 to 11 ms at every size

fix: an open that scanned 64 MiB or more after a crash checkpoints it (ckpt_at was set to the scan end, so repeated kills rescanned an ever longer tail); group kill test reopen p50 460 to 35 ms; no format change
cells, number formats and formulas as shapes (25 formulas, 12 shapes) render csv, json, md exact 24/24; 22/22 input edits carried exact to every computed cell; 0.12 ms against 872 ms for LibreOffice
one paragraph edit to 64 md files and their html and docx (192 endpoints): splices 194 ms against 8,477 ms re-render, 128/128 exact; kernel adds 25 KB with md render-runs against 47 KB plain
summaries per fragment kept fresh through 22 edits: 7.5 ms reading 5.7 KB, exact, against 481 ms reading 4.8 MB; a 64-file edit 1.55 ms and 117 B; left stale, $222,240 off after 22 edits
goal-scoped queries read only matching fragments: 0.33 ms and 8.4 KB against 15 ms and 218 KB per query, exact 12/12; summary-only query reads 0 bytes
workbook aggregates kept fresh by re-evaluating only the edited workbook's IR: exact 22/22, 0.14 ms against 0.32 ms; stale aggregates wrong after 18/22 edits
churn took only three of six pack names; one shared pack_options table and two harness tests, so churn packs-filter runs
summaries stored as WASM derivations in a view graph beside files: exact through 22 edits, gc and restart; 2.3 ms per edit, 63 KB written; no query gain without an index
word lists in the view: first query after restart 0.73 ms reading 21 KB against 21 ms and 163 KB; 8x the bytes written per edit; lists beat node postings
60 kills during view upkeep on FsStore and PackStore: every head's view matches its files, fsck clean
18,000 fragments: stored 7 ms and 2 KB per edit; postings first query 29 ms against 548, at 60x the bytes per edit and 3.5x storage; found E190
open pack prefix lookups by binary search over a lazily sorted id list: ledger load 4,251 to 93 ms at 38,862 objects; open and point reads as on main

opt-in IR codec (src/ir.rs): cells and line skeletons; templates alone tie xz on reports (1.03), 0.69 on md+csv+json exports, 1.25 on prose

csv/json/md of one table stored once by a cell diff: exports 0.483 of xz; real tables 0.927 with numbers and siblings, no columns
IR parts in the kernel: drift reports 10,362 against 27,657 B for files, ingest 218 against 3,400 ms; one-file read needs a full decode (12 ms); prose 7% larger
column query 0.08 ms reading 2 KB; a layout edit across 218 reports 624 against 49,608 B; layout and outlier drift flagged at ingest; 5/5 stale csv exports found
IR in blocks of 20 to 100 reports in the kernel: drift 0.72 to 1.13 of xz with 1 to 7 ms one-report reads, against files 1.641 at 0.03 ms; keyframe blocks save 4 to 14%
files under 10% cell bytes stored raw: prose texts 1.249 to 1.000 of xz, mixed folder 1.013 to 0.826, reports and tables unchanged
cells diffed against the most similar of the last 16 files: drift blocks of 20 in the kernel 0.984 to 0.759 of xz with 0.40 ms reads; shuffled drift 0.906 to 0.770; window 1 worse
each column learns which earlier cell of its line determines it: drift 0.591 to 0.543 of xz, exports 0.483 to 0.448; decode 11 to 26 ms; no gain in blocks of 20
streams sorted by key: row-key layouts 4 to 8% smaller; best overall changes only on reports-random 0.654 to 0.638 of xz; no change in blocks

dependencies read out of the IR templates (link determines lag, status, numbers); blips find 87 to 91% of errors put in covered columns with 93 to 98% precision; found a duplicate id in the generated data

one column of 300 reports from its stream alone: 0.6 to 1.1 ms against 18 to 25 ms reading the files, parts in the kernel at 0.82 (drift) and 0.64 (random) of xz; needs siblings, nearest and predict off
number columns predict last value plus last step beside a key: drift 0.543 to 0.505 of xz, exports 0.448 to 0.436; decode 28 to 37 ms; blocks of 20 0.734 to 0.713
column queries with predict and step on: drift parts in the kernel 0.548 of xz with queries in 13 ms (0.819 and 1 ms without); random 0.619; predictor learning is the cost
same bytes (parity hashes equal); drift predict+step decode 36 to 23 ms, column query 13.7 to 4.1 ms; queryable store at 0.548 of xz now answers in 4 ms

real files: registry 0.966 of xz (columns only; predict and step add nothing), cases text folder 1.08 to 1.44 of xz, loses on every file kind; schema finds ACTIVITY DESC from NAICS; column query slower than splitting the files

per kind of file (extension and first-line template), IR or plain, judged by xz -6: worst case 1.000 of xz (was 1.115); cases text 1.105 to 0.995, cases+drift 1.041 to 0.940; generated corpora unchanged; encode 0.5 to 13 s

per stream choice of number deltas, predicted and stepped cells, judged by xz -6: registry 1.000 to 0.961 with route (best untuned 0.966); random 0.644 to 0.633; drift 0.504; encode up to 47 s on 10.8 MB
strings written out in full as a tune choice: registry 0.961 to 0.960, every other best unchanged; 1.5 to 1.7x tune encode time; the dictionary is not why the IR trails a plain transpose (0.953)
CSV rows stably sorted by the best key column, key kept in file order (no permutation): registry 0.961 to 0.942 of xz (sorted by NAICS); Python prototype on a plain transpose 0.909
CSV tables stored plain by column when route picks it: registry 0.942 to 0.930 of xz with sort (0.930 with columns alone, 14 s encode); not queryable by column
transpose leaves out the quotes of a column quoted in every row: registry with sort 0.930 to 0.911 of xz (from 0.966 at E207), transpose alone 0.954
route and tune judged on large files cut to a 1 MB sample: every size and route choice the same on 6 corpora; registry tuned encode 43 to 7 s, columns 13 to 5 s

six settings on 9 corpora: predict, step, tuned best or tied on 7 (drift 0.504, random 0.630, registry 0.911) and never worse than xz; siblings and nearest win on exports (0.459) and tables (0.936) and cost the reports 3 to 8%; row keys never help

route also judges per kind of file whether to diff against a base: one setting best or tied on all 9 corpora (drift 0.504, random 0.630, exports 0.458, tables 0.936, registry 0.911), never worse than xz; untuned within 0.015 at 2 to 4x faster

E216 setting in the kernel against the files in the kernel: drift 0.303, exports 0.228, random 0.502, cases (real) 0.672, registry (real) 0.916; blocks of 50 with keyframe keep most (0.28 to 0.82) with 1 to 10 ms reads

damaged packs and blocks under four settings never panic (16,000 changes, release and debug); fixed an overflow in the E211 sorted-table check that crashed release builds on a huge count; deltas wrap; ir_parity identical

sample judges many small files on four runs of neighbours: 18 MB of reports encode in 0.8 to 1.1 s untuned (was 2.4 to 4.7 s, same sizes), tuned 2 to 6x faster and up to 0.014 larger; drift at 3,000 files 0.31 of xz

registry cut into row groups (prototype): 10,000 rows 0.981 alone, 0.955 after group 0, against 0.912 whole; below about 4,000 rows groups are larger than xz over the files; reads scale only with group size; 10,000-row groups after a keyframe are the knee
each block's raw part as its own store entry: at most 0.012 better (cases, blocks of 50: 0.811 vs 0.819), up to 0.049 worse elsewhere; blocks keep raw text with their streams

E216 setting on the north corpora, text files as one IR pack and office or pdf left to the kernel: cases 0.817, multiformat 0.969, tables 1.199 (cross-format sharing lost); text alone 0.66 to 0.73 of the kernel; keeping the pack only where smaller would give north about 0.281 (from 0.3035)

files kept readable as IR pack members (ir-member and ir-block-member builtins, Repo::put_ir, put_ir_blocks): north judged 0.914 against 0.920 for short records alone (0.993); per-member records and a zstd pack (planner charges a decode per member) eat the gain; not worth turning on
prototype: cases raw text in blocks of 50 compressed after block 0 is 1.222 of xz over all files, against 1.531 alone (a fifth less); worth building as a keyframe dictionary for raw parts

raw_keyframe: later blocks' raw parts as zstd frames with block 0's raw as dictionary; in the kernel worse (cases blocks of 20 0.833 to 1.249, of 50 0.819 to 0.869), the store already compresses blocks better; option kept, off
